primary.title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog
primary.summary: Perplexity is launching a Monitor API that searches the web on a schedule and alerts agents via webhook only when relevant changes occur. Its own decision model filters out unimportant results. For Perplexity, the API is part of a broader strategy to stand out from an increasingly interchangeable chatbot business through developer tools. The article Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog appeared first on The Decoder.

primary.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
primary.summary: A new real-world test puts AI coding agents in a simulated developer job with colleagues, project boards, and incomplete handoffs, where they have to keep developing software on their own and reliably close open tickets in a messy daily workflow. Even Opus 5.5 and Astra fall far short, solving fewer than one in ten tasks completely. The models finish clear, standalone assignments quickly, but they lose track as autonomous developers. The article AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace appeared first on The Decoder.

primary.title: Nvidia researchers argue huge AI context windows are a dead end
primary.summary: Nvidia researchers argue that language models often don't need their full context windows—which are slow, expensive, and prone to errors—and propose an alternative. In tests, periodic summaries and targeted keyword search usually matched full-context results at a fraction of the cost. The team even proposes a new class of models that works with short notes instead of long context. The article Nvidia researchers argue huge AI context windows are a dead end appeared first on The Decoder.
